author: motion_reconstruction
scope: Read-only first-hit/occlusion diagnosis of the held 41,562-triangle GLB f0418366. No quality score. Source may have changed during the author repair; geometric evidence below applies to this exact exported GLB.
coordinates: canonical runtime car coordinates: +X forward, +Y up, +Z right, metres; car origin at wheel-contact center floor

method.loader: installed three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js, actual GLB parsed in Node; all matrixWorld transforms updated
method.pixel_grid: raycast projected image samples x840..1050,y555..690,step5 through the actual GLB from the current Car-view pose. Rays identify first visible model surfaces; screenshot RGB is measured at the corresponding pixel. Lighting itself was not simulated.
method.LED_visibility: For each of the 82 actual luminous BodyShell triangles, raycast to its centroid and compare first-hit distance to expected centroid distance, tolerance .0001m.

conclusions.finding: The old vertical belt cap no longer blocks the horizontal mouth view.
conclusions.evidence: At height .18 through .40, all17 columns first hit FrontRecessBack. At .45/.50,15 columns hit the back and2 hit side jambs. Back/jamb material is IntakeAbsorbent. The next cut-body/belt cap lies behind the back at X1.8114.

conclusions.finding: A surviving horizontal belt cut floor and the broad splitter top produce the gray tray in the elevated Car view.
conclusions.implication: Changing or lowering only FrontOpeningJambs did not change these two larger first-visible carbon surfaces. From above they occlude the intended floor and expose broad lit tops.
conclusions.repair: Clear the belt cutter floor below the intended cavity floor, and replace the broad splitter tray by the designed narrow lip. Use intended cavity material/AO consistently on all remaining interior first-visible surfaces. Author reports these source changes are building; not yet evaluated here.

conclusions.finding: The actual recess back is darker than the tray, but remains a visible blue-gray wall under the current environment.
conclusions.evidence: Pixel-matched back-wall medianRGB[40,54,68] versus belt-floor[93,110,128] and splitter[96,114,133]. No wrong bright material was found on the back.
conclusions.inference: The current material/lighting combination still supplies visible indirect/specular response. Recess depth alone does not occlude image-based ambient light in the installed forward PBR shader; no AO map was found. Once the geometry floors are fixed, a locally controlled AO/environment response may be needed for the very dark source cavity. This is a shading inference, not an isolated GPU lighting measurement.
local_shader_evidence: node_modules/three/src/renderers/shaders/ShaderChunk/aomap_fragment.glsl.js:5-21 applies ambient/specular occlusion only when an AO map is enabled

conclusions.finding: Near-side LED regions are bright and visible; the dark slit is the adjacent pocket border. The far-side lamp is geometrically occluded in the current oblique Car view.
conclusions.implication: Increasing LED emission does not fix an occluded far-side patch or create contrast against a saturated white hood. The current lamp topology includes an8mm cap recess that makes oblique self-occlusion stronger.
conclusions.repair: Consider a near-flush1-2mm lens depth, with an intentional narrow dark border, while retaining source-shaped luminous area. Check from a lower/frontward source-like view as well as current Car view; pure-front rays see all82 luminous centroids.

notes: The scene ground/apron is absent from this local-model raycast; all identified gray tray hits are actual car geometry, not the stage floor.
Material exports, colors, metalness, roughness and emissive factors are read from actual loaded mesh materials.
